title: Gilgamesh's Dream of a Companion
subtitle: A dream foreshadows the arrival of Enkidu

dream.work: An Old Babylonian Version of the Gilgamesh Epic
dream.author: Anonymous
dream.translator: Morris Jastrow and Albert T. Clay
dream.locator: Pennsylvania Tablet · Column I; Pennsylvania Tablet · Column I, normalized characters 841-1231
dream.excerpt: My likeness I have seen in the streets [Of Erech] of the plazas. An axe was brandished, and They gathered about him; And the axe made him angry. I saw him and I rejoiced, I loved him as a woman, I embraced him. I took him and regarded him As my brother." The mother of Gish, who knows all things, [Spoke to Gish]: ["O Gish, the man whom thou sawest,] [Whom thou didst embrace like a woman].
dream.note: Verbatim translation from the named Old Babylonian tablet witness in this edited edition. Brackets and question marks signal textual restoration or uncertainty.

narrativeBlocks.title: A second dream
narrativeBlocks.body: In the Pennsylvania Tablet translation, Gilgamesh describes a dream to his mother: he sees a likeness in Erech, an axe, and a figure he embraces as a brother.

narrativeBlocks.title: Gilgamesh names the dream
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Jastrow and Clay's tablet translation; whitespace normalized): “My likeness I have seen in the streets [Of Erech] of the plazas. An axe was brandished, and They gathered about him; And the axe made him angry. I saw him and I rejoiced, I loved him as a woman, I embraced him. I took him and regarded him As my brother." The mother of Gish, who knows all things, [Spoke to Gish]: ["O Gish, the man whom thou sawest,] [Whom thou didst embrace like a woman].”

narrativeBlocks.title: A mother's interpretation
narrativeBlocks.body: The surviving lines show Gilgamesh's mother interpreting the dream as a man who will become his companion. The bracketed words signal editorial restorations in this translation.

narrativeBlocks.title: A fragment, not a complete epic
narrativeBlocks.body: The Pennsylvania Tablet is an Old Babylonian fragment in a modern edited translation by Jastrow and Clay. Its missing or restored wording should remain visible.

narrativeBlocks.title: The companion is anticipated
narrativeBlocks.body: The dream gives the relationship a narrative beginning before the two men meet. It is a scene in this tablet witness, not evidence that every version uses identical wording.
